items.note: The page follows the paper's proof of Lemma lem:signed-ring-product stage by stage: signed evaluation at $B_0=2^{4p}$, four products of absolute values, centered-residue extraction with a carry, wrapping modulo $y^r+1$, truncation, and the cost total. It also spells out the separation bound $|h_j|\le r2^{2p}<2^{3p}<B_0/2$, which the assignment flagged as left to the reader.

The page writes $f=2^{-p}(a+ib)$, $g=2^{-p}(c+ie)$ and gets the component bound $2^p$ from 'coefficients are $2^{-p}$ times Gaussian integers of modulus at most $2^p$'. It states only 'Assume $r<2^p$'. The facts that $r=2^\ell$ with $\ell\ge1$ and that $p\ge2$ come only through the ring $\mathcal R_r$, which requires $r\ge2$ to be a power of two.
'By the geometric sum, $|A_u|\le2^p(B_0^r-1)/(B_0-1)<B_0^r/2$, so its magnitude fits in $4pr$ bits.' This matches the paper. The last inequality is asserted without a check, as it is in the paper.

The page explains why absolute values are multiplied ('The multiplier takes nonnegative integers') and how each sign is restored. It gives $A_aA_c=(ac)(B_0)=\sum_{j<2r}h_jB_0^j$ with the padding $h_{2r-1}=0$, as the paper does.

The first inequality is justified: 'Each $h_j$ sums at most $r$ products of coefficients of size at most $2^p$'. The second uses the assumed $r<2^p$. The third, $2^{3p}<B_0/2$, needs $p\ge2$, which is left implicit. The identification by centered residue is then shown in the extraction paragraph.

The page gives the same carry recurrence, the bound $-B_0<u_j+\gamma_j<B_0$ (like the paper, without noting $|u_j|\le2^p$) and the telescoped identity. It goes further than the paper in showing why $\gamma_r=-1$ exactly when $A_u<0$ and why complement-and-increment yields $|A_u|$.

The page uses the paper's centered extraction and the paper's induction. 'If $\widehat h_i=h_i$ for $i<j$, then $\sum_{i<j}q_iB_0^i=\sum_{i<j}h_iB_0^i+\rho_jB_0^j$, so $q_j+\rho_j\equiv h_j$', and then the separation bound gives $\widehat h_j=h_j$. Two arguments are compressed: the carry bound ('since $q_j+\rho_j\in[0,B_0]$') leaves out the inductive hypothesis and the fact that centering subtracts $0$ or $B_0$, and the paper's final-carry check $0=\rho_J+\varepsilon$ is omitted. Neither is needed for correctness.

'The real and imaginary numerator streams are $ac-be$ and $ae+bc$. Since $y^{j+r}=-y^j$, reduce modulo $y^r+1$ by subtracting the coefficient at $j+r$ from the one at $j$.' This matches the paper, and the missing top coefficient is handled by the earlier padding.

The page gives the paper's index-pairing argument (exactly one $j_2$ for each $j_1$, with sign $\pm$), which yields $|H_j|\le r2^{2p}$. It then finds that each coefficient $2^{-2p}H_j/r$ of $fg/r$ has modulus at most $1$. This is the same bound the paper's triangle inequality gives.

dropped: the truncation does not increase modulus ($\|Q_pz\|_\infty\le\|z\|_\infty$), so the output is itself a disk grid polynomial
the output is written as signed $w$-bit two's-complement words in the component format, at cost $O(rw)=O(rp)$ using $w\le C_wp$
items.note: The page derives the truncation formula ($Q_p(2^{-2p}H_j/r)$ by a right shift of $p+\log_2r$ bits), the error ('Each part loses less than $2^{-p}$, so the error is less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$') and the cost (four products on inputs of at most $4pr$ bits, with every other stage linear). It does not show that the returned polynomial stays in the disk, and it does not cover the output-format conversion.
